clips.send: Pins (键 jiàn). Bronze pins the parts turn on. Two pins go right through the housing and the stock.
clips.text: Pins (键 jiàn)。Bronze pins the parts turn on。Two pins go right through the housing and the stock.

clips.send: Crossbow square (kneeling and standing). The front corner of Pit 2. Kneeling crossbowmen in the middle, standing archers around them. One idea: one group shoots while the other reloads, so the arrows never stop. An L-shaped pit with four mixed units; roughly 1,300 figures and 80+ chariots (approximate).

clips.send: Armoured infantry. Filling the long corridors of Pit 1. The main body of the army: thousands of soldiers in armour, in columns four wide. They carried long bronze weapons such as spears and halberds (戈, 矛, 戟). About 230 m times 62 m (755 times 203 ft) — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about 6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

clips.send: Teeth (牙 yá). Two bronze hooks that catch and hold the string. When you cock the crossbow, the string is pulled back and locks behind the teeth. The teeth and the sight are one piece that turns on a bronze pin.

clips.send: Battle of Guiling. 353 BC. Guiling (one view: today’s Changyuan, Henan Province). Qi (Tian Ji, Sun Bin) vs Wei (Pang Juan 庞涓). Qi wins; Wei’s attempt to swallow Zhao fails. The plan lives on as the idiom “besiege Wei to rescue Zhao” (围魏救赵). 避实而击虚. Avoid the enemy’s strong points; strike the weak ones.

clips.send: Dont mix up: A crossbow (弩) is not just a bow (弓): the trigger lets you hold the string drawn and aim calmly, so less strength and training are needed.

clips.send: Battle of Chibi (Red Cliffs). 208 AD. Chibi on the Yangtze River (one view: today’s Chibi City, Hubei Province). Sun Quan + Liu Bei (刘备) vs Cao Cao. The allies win with far fewer men. Cao Cao retreats north; the three-way split of China (三国鼎立) begins to take shape. 兵者, 诡道也. War is a game of deception: when strong, look weak; when near, look far away.

clips.send: String (弦 xián). Pushes the bolt forward when released. A complete Qin crossbow found in the pits still had traces of a string thought to be made of animal tendon.

clips.send: Stock (臂 bì). The wooden body with a groove for the bolt. The wood has rotted away in the pits; the bronze parts survived.

clips.send: Dont mix up: The Terracotta Army pits are not the First Emperor’s tomb. They lie about 1.5 km (1 mile) east of the tomb mound, which has never been opened.

clips.send: Trigger (悬刀 xuándāo). The hanging “knife” you pull to shoot. A small pull on a long lever releases a huge force: that is leverage.

clips.send: Linzi. Today: Zibo, Shandong. One of the biggest cities in the world 2,300 years ago — so crowded that “raising your sleeves makes shade”.

clips.send: Sear (牛 niú, also 钩心). The hidden middle link that holds the teeth in place. It sits between the teeth and the trigger, inside the housing. Pull the trigger and the sear drops — the teeth are free to swing down.

clips.send: Bolt (矢 shǐ). A short arrow with a bronze three-sided head. Tens of thousands of bronze arrowheads have been found with the Terracotta Army.

clips.send: Command post. Pit 3, the smallest pit. Only 68 figures: guards lining the walls, facing each other, and one chariot. It is thought to be the headquarters that commanded the army in Pits 1 and 2. A small U-shaped pit with 68 figures and one chariot: the command post.

clips.send: Sight (望山 wàngshān). The aiming blade — like the sight on a rifle. It sticks up when the crossbow is cocked. Line it up with the target. Some Han-dynasty sights even had a scale of marks for different distances.

clips.send: Battle of the Fei River. 383 AD. The Fei River near Shouyang (today’s Shou County, Anhui Province). Eastern Jin (Xie Shi, Xie Xuan) vs Former Qin (Fu Jian 苻坚). Eastern Jin wins with far fewer men. Former Qin falls apart and the north splits again; the south stays safe and keeps developing. 上下同欲者胜. The side whose leaders and soldiers want the same thing will win.

clips.send: Battle of Muye. c. 1046 BC. Muye, near today’s Xinxiang, Henan Province. Zhou + allied tribes (King Wu) vs Shang (King Zhou 纣王). Zhou wins. The Shang dynasty falls and the Western Zhou begins, with its capital at Haojing. 不战而屈人之兵, 善之善者也. The very best victory makes the enemy give up without a fight.

clips.send: Battle of Guandu. 200 AD. Guandu, northeast of today’s Zhongmou, Henan Province. Cao Cao vs Yuan Shao (袁绍). Cao Cao wins with far fewer men — a famous “small beats big” battle. It lays the foundation for Cao Cao to unite the north. 军无辎重则亡, 无粮食则亡. An army without supply wagons is lost; an army without food is lost.

clips.send: 淝水之战。383年。淝水（今安徽寿县一带）。东晋（谢石、谢玄）对 前秦（苻坚）。东晋以少胜多。前秦很快瓦解，北方重新陷入分裂；南方保持安定，经济继续发展。上下同欲者胜。上下一条心、目标一致的一方能取胜。
